brief: A media write-up of a note from Goldman Sachs One-Delta desk head Rich Privorotsky, plus one Goldman research call. Privorotsky's chain: cost per token is compressing hard, so consumption must grow extraordinarily fast just to offset it. Silicon Data's expenditure-weighted token index fell 29% in August to about $0.97 per million tokens, a record low and more than 50% off the May peak near $2.05. JPMorgan's data-center note had OpenRouter volume up roughly 47% month over month while dollar spend rose only about 7%, and H100 rental pricing is falling, so volume is not paying for the price cut. Add open-weight competition and inference shifting to cheaper local hardware, and Privorotsky says he struggles with per-token pricing as a durable end state. Unless capability jumps radically, with OpenAI's unlaunched Astra named as the possible exception, periods of compute oversupply become plausible. That meets financed capex: five rated hyperscalers projected near $737 billion of 2026 capex, about 38% of revenue, and 78 of 91 hyperscaler bonds issued in 2026 traded below issue by late August. Separately Jim Schneider reiterates Buy on Broadcom. Three counter-arguments are listed, none rescuing multiples.
